cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Bippalapadra situated in the district of Suvarṇamañjarī It further registers the grant of half of the revenue from the village to a group of temples dedicated to Hari, Haradēva, Vināyaka and the divine mothers, which were erected on the outskirts of the city by Śivarudra who was a karpaṭin i.e., an ascetic dressed in rags The donee of the other half was a maṭhapati, whose name has not been specified The lipikāra was Vakula, son of Viṭṭhaka. The dūtaka was Prince Jāika. Published in Ibid., pp. 212 ff. and plate.

cells.place: Kanatru. - Stone lying below the mango tree in the backyard of Jamal-u-ddin Pāsha.
cells.date: Śaka 947, Krōdhana, Chaitra, Peṭṭale-devasa = 1025 A.D., March 17(?).
cells.remarks: Gives an eulogy of the chief Malaparāja. States that the village Kaḍabavaḷḷi was bestowed upon a person (name lost), who was the son of a nāḷgamuṇḍa of Maṇale-300 division, as koḍage. cells.place: Rāmanāthapura, - Outer wall of the garbhagṛiha of the Rāmanātha temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1173, Sādhāraṇa, Kārttika śu. 1, Sunday. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of lands by Kallaiya, son of Rāmarāsa of Kāśyapa-gōtra for the person tending the flower gardens as jīvita and for the worship of the deity Rāmanātha. It refers to the donor as an officer under Baṇṇappa, the administrator of Koṅga-nāḍu. The latter is mentioned as the son of Rudra belonging to Viśvāmitra-gōtra and a subordinate of samdhivigrahi Boṇṇama-daṇḍanāyaka. Boṇṇama is described as the Sevaṇa-kaṭṭu-diśāpaṭṭa and a mahāpradhāna of the king.

cells.date: Śaka 1174, Virōdhikṛit, Āśvīdha śu. 1, Thursday = 1251 A.D., June 22. The tithi ended on the previous day.
cells.remarks: In continuation of (No. 147) above. Records the grant of lands by Kallaiya for the person tending the garden and for the worship of the deity Rāmanāthadēva. Also registers the assignment of income from taxes collected from the village to this deity by the same donor. The gift is stated to have been entrusted to Sōvaṇṇa, the son-in-law of Nākaruṇpa and Vijayappa, the śrīkaraṇa of Koṅga-nāḍu. This was attested by Sōvaṇṇa.

cells.place: Stone set up towards the south, near the outer wall of the ranga-maṇḍapa of the same temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1174, Virōdhikṛit, Puṣya śu. 10, Thursday = 1252 A.D., December 12.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of village Māvantru for the offerings to god Rāmanātha by Bappadēva, Sōmadēva, rāyasa-kūśugal and others on the plea made by the temple priests Śivajīya, Māḍadēva, Kālajīya, Appajīya, Arasajīya and Gōvaṇṇa. Earlier, a grant of 72 (she and he) buffaloes is stated to have been made by both Sōmadēva and Bappadēva who were ruling over Śrīraṅgapaṭṭaṇa as feudatories of the king. It is stated that that grant was made as the earlier gift was not sufficient to meet the expenditure of the temple. So a fresh application was made to that effect. Ibid. Published in pp. carr., Vol. V, Ag. 53.

cells.date: Śaka 1197, Yuva, Āśvayuja śu. 10, Tuesday = 1275 A.D., October 1.
cells.remarks: Records the assignment of the income from taxes on loom, goat, etc., at Dēvarahaḷḷi for the perpetual lamp and amṛitapaḍi to god Rāmanātha jointly by Hampanna, Gummaṇṇa and Basavaṇṇa, the customs officers of Koṅga-nāḍu. Also it records the gift of income from taxes, oil, etc., for the perpetual lamp to the same deity, by various persons. The gifts were entrusted to the temple priests, to the kumbiāra, paṁchakāra, etc., of the village. Ibid., Ag. 54.

cells.location: Heragu, Belur Taluk, Hassan District.
cells.place: Stone kept in the State Archaeological Museum.
cells.date: Śaka 1139, Īśvara, Māgha śu. 15, Monday, Lunar eclipse = 1218 A.D., January 13. The weekday was Saturday.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the king and traces the parentage of Jayabhaṭṭa-nāyaka. Records the installation of the god Jaita-Nārāyaṇadēva and registers the gift of a village Aṇehaḷḷi along with 40 gadyāṇas. It was made free from all imposts. The donee mahāpāsāyia Jaibhaṭṭaya-nāyaka is stated to have migrated from Bhadrāhu in Gula-vishaya, a sub-division of Krama-rājya in Kāśmīra-rāshṭra. Also registers the grant of money and lands for the various services to the same deity by the mahājanas of Heragu village. Published in Ep. Carn., Vol. V. (Old edition), Hn. 61.

cells.place: Stone set up to the south of Gōvindēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the king Gōvindarāja and his mahāmātya Gōvindamayya (also called Gōvindarāja). It also gives the eulogy of this chief, his wife Sāntave and the śrīkaraṇa Būchirāja. Records the construction of a Śaṅkara temple and the consecration of the image of Śiva in an agrahāra in Sīge-nāḍu by Gōvindamayya. He is stated to have endowed lands for the daily worship of the deity Gōvindēśvara, for the feeding of the brāhmaṇas, and for repairs to the temple. The gift was entrusted to Vibhāraṇapaṇḍitadēva. In characters of the 13th century A.D. Ibid., Hn. 72.

cells.place: Stone set up to the south of the Kalēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the king and mahāpradhāna Nākimayya. Refers to the construction of the temple of Nākiśvara at Kōravamgala, an agrahāra in Sige-nāḍu, and registers the gift of lands as sarvanamasya to the deity Śiva installed there, for the daily worship, services like ārōpaṇa, for the feeding of the brāhmaṇas and for the repairs to the temple by the chief. cells.remarks: Madras. - An ornamental plough preserved in the Government Museum, Madras. Findspot: Not known. This plough is made of copper measuring 12 cms at the handle and 13.5 cms. at the triangular tapering shaft. It weighs 770 gms. Records a gift of the banner (mēḷikkodi) to Kachchip-pāṇḍaram of the Periyaṇāṭṭumaḍam at Kāñchīpuram by the Periyaṇāṭṭumaḍam of Ā-Toṇḍaimaṇḍalam, symbolising his rights to the revenue collected from among the members of the group on occasions and at stipulated rates.

cells.remarks: Records an order (ōlai) of the chief Vikrama-pāṇḍya Toṇḍamāṇ issued to the tāṇattār of Rāśipuram Kāyilāyam-uḍaiyā-nāyaṇār temple at Rāśipuram for depositing into the temple treasury, the levy amount at the rate of three paṇam per kuḍi (tenant) who came to settle down at the tirumadaivīḷāgam of the temple, of two paṇam per kuḍi who had settled down at Kiḷakkudi Veḷḷarukkai and of ten paṇam imposed as fine (deṇḍam) on those who committed offences. Also specifies about the execution of the order of the mudaḷi for the deposition of the money and the sale of maṇai allotted by the dēvaraḍiyār in the tirumadaivīḷāgam by the sabhai, the nāḍu and the nagaram with effect from the month of Tai in the 7th regnal year of the chief. cells.place: Vaijāpur. - Headstone of a grave in the compound of the Jāmi' mosque.
cells.remarks: Indicates the grave of the martyr Ḥusain Khān, who attained martyrdom on the first date. Further states that on the second date, 21 bīghā of land situated in the town of Vījāpūr (Vaijāpur) was allotted to Shēr Khān, son of the deceased by the (Āṣaf Jāhī) government for meeting the expenditure incurred on incense and flowers (for the grave). The land is now in the name of Puṭlī Bī and Chānd Bī and Puṭlī Bī is now the actual possessor. It was written on the third date and the (text) was got engraved by the members of the Committee for Religious Affairs whose names are mentioned as Mīr Ḥasan 'Alī, Pensioner, Amīn Karongirī (Tax Collector), Ghulām Maḥmūd, Advocate, 'Isā Khān, Advocate, Qāẓī Amīnu'd-Dīn, Advocate and Muḥammad Hāshim, Advocate.

cells.place: Tomb of Nawwab Darwish Ali in the locality called Lakra. Marble slab in the north wall.
cells.date: (1) A.H. 1131, Muharram 14= 1718 A.D., November 26 (2) A.H. 1152, Dhu'l-Qa'da 15=1740 A.D., February 2 (3) A.H. 1208, Shawwal 2= 1794 A.D., May 25.
cells.remarks: States that this is the grave of Nawwab Darwish 'Ali Khan Bahadur who achieved martyrdom in the battle fought against the Barh (i.e. Sadat-i-Barha) on the first date. The deceased is stated to have held the rank of 2050 and 'Ardi-i-Mukarrari and Deputy Mir-i-Bakhshiship of the Royal Cavalry under Muhammad Farrukh Siyar and Muhammad Shah Bahadur. Also states that the whole pargana of Amroha was assigned to meet the expenditure on his kitchen. The text further states that the grave on his right is that of his eldest son Ghulam Muhyi Din Khan-i-Thani (the Second), while that on his left is of his second son namely Muhammad Fakhr'ud-Din Khan, both of whom had achieved martyrdom on the second date while fighting in battle against Nadir Shah (of Persia). It also states that the grave of his younger son Muhammad Shams'ud-Din Khan who died on the third date is outside the Tomb proper. In late characters.
